item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-17
item.description: On 2026-11-16 DeepSeek imposed the first hard usage limits on its free web and app tier since the company was founded: single-input context compressed to roughly 40,000 characters, long conversations inactive for more than seven days no longer continuable, and a daily cap beyond which the page displays 'server busy, usage limit reached'. The occasion is a year of 57 incidents of outage or degradation on the company's own status page, including a five-hour global outage on 15 October and a second large one on 7 November; the mechanism is given precisely by 21st Century Business Herald and it is not demand: an agentic office assistant, the largest third-party proxy for DeepSeek's API, went from 32.4 million monthly actives in September to 8.36 billion monthly interactions, and an agent turn costs about four times a conversational one — fifteen times under multi-agent orchestration, with OpenRouter reporting that 80 per cent of token consumption is now agentic. On the same day a different kind of measurement appeared on the other side of the ecosystem: two regional newsrooms recorded COSCon'26's closing numbers — 1,000-plus attendees on day one, 600,000-plus views on a provincial news app, a nine-level OPC capability standard, the first 'open source mentor' credentials, and a youth track whose youngest speaker was nine years old — and an industry report chapter published this fortnight recorded that China's public open-source money is visible as per-project caps and rates, while its award notices, and the individual maintainer those awards do not pay, are not visible at all. Read together, the three documents measure the demand side of Chinese AI open source with accounting precision and the supply side by counting people who attended.
